answer.text: The survey was completed by 150 students. The main findings show that 60 percent of respondents sleep fewer than eight hours. Furthermore, the percentage is higher in the final year, where it reaches 70 percent. Only a minority of students, 18 percent, use a phone after midnight; nevertheless, this group reports the worst sleep. It appears that late phone use may be linked to poor sleep, although the survey cannot prove this. These results are consistent with the national survey, which stated that teenagers sleep too little. Therefore, the school may wish to consider a later start. Notably, the highest figure is found in the final year. More research is needed to confirm these findings.
accepted: The survey was completed by 150 students. The main findings show that 60 percent of respondents sleep fewer than eight hours. Furthermore, the percentage is higher in the final year, where it reaches 70 percent. Only a minority of students, 18 percent, use a phone after midnight; nevertheless, this group reports the worst sleep. It appears that late phone use may be linked to poor sleep, although the survey cannot prove this. These results are consistent with the national survey, which stated that teenagers sleep too little. Therefore, the school may wish to consider a later start. Notably, the highest figure is found in the final year. More research is needed to confirm these findings.

According to the survey of 150 students, 60 percent sleep fewer than eight hours, and the figure rises to 70 percent in the final year. Moreover, a minority of respondents, 18 percent, use a phone after midnight; however, they report the worst sleep. There is some evidence that phones may affect sleep, but the data do not show that they are the cause. The findings are consistent with the national survey, which stated that teenagers do not sleep enough. Therefore, it is recommended that the school should consider a later start. Notably, the figure is highest in the final year. The percentage of students affected could be higher in other schools.

feedback.es: La sección combina cifras, tres conectores formales, una fuente y al menos dos afirmaciones matizadas (it appears that, may, tend to).

origin.text: Encuesta escolar sobre el sueño (150 estudiantes): el 60 % duerme menos de ocho horas; en último curso, el 70 %; el 18 % usa el móvil después de medianoche y duerme peor. La encuesta nacional afirma que los adolescentes duermen poco. Escribe entre 110 y 180 palabras: tres conectores formales (furthermore, nevertheless, therefore…), la fuente y dos afirmaciones matizadas.

prompt.es: Elige la versión formal y matizada del hallazgo sobre el uso del móvil.

I think phones are terrible because 18 percent use them at night.

feedback.es: Appear to sleep worse es prudente y neutro; las otras versiones afirman una causa o usan un tono personal.

es: Elaborar un mini informe sobre el transporte escolar y presentarlo en un resumen oral de un minuto con punto clave, cautela y recomendación.

teaching.en: This report gives an overview of how students commute to school.
teaching.es: Este informe ofrece una visión general de cómo se desplazan los estudiantes al colegio.
teaching.explanationEs: Give an overview introduce el panorama general; commute es el trayecto diario al colegio o al trabajo.
segments: This report gives an overview of
how students commute to school.
teaching.audioText: This report gives an overview of how students commute to school.

teaching.en: I will outline the main findings in one minute.
teaching.es: Esbozaré los principales resultados en un minuto.
teaching.explanationEs: I will outline… es la fórmula oral para anunciar el resumen; cada frase oral es corta.
segments: I will outline the main
findings in one minute.
teaching.audioText: I will outline the main findings in one minute.

teaching.en: The key point is that most students depend on the school bus.
teaching.es: El punto clave es que la mayoría de los estudiantes depende del autobús escolar.
teaching.explanationEs: The key point is that… da la idea central; en una presentación oral se dice una sola vez y se repite al final.
segments: The key point is that most
students depend on the school bus.
teaching.audioText: The key point is that most students depend on the school bus.

teaching.en: To conclude, it appears that late buses are the main problem, although more evidence is needed.
teaching.es: Para concluir, parece que los autobuses tardíos son el problema principal, aunque hace falta más evidencia.
teaching.explanationEs: To conclude cierra el resumen; se mantiene la cautela de las clases anteriores (it appears, more evidence is needed).
segments: To conclude, it appears that late buses are
the main problem, although more evidence is needed.
teaching.audioText: To conclude, it appears that late buses are the main problem, although more evidence is needed.

teaching.en: We recommend a second morning bus, so the commute would be shorter.
teaching.es: Recomendamos un segundo autobús por la mañana, así el trayecto sería más corto.
teaching.explanationEs: We recommend + sustantivo o -ing; el condicional would dice el efecto esperado.
segments: We recommend a second morning bus,
so the commute would be shorter.
teaching.audioText: We recommend a second morning bus, so the commute would be shorter.

teaching.en: To keep the summary concise, I will mention only two findings.
teaching.es: Para que el resumen sea conciso, mencionaré solo dos resultados.
teaching.explanationEs: Un resumen oral breve elige los dos o tres datos más importantes; no los repite todos.
segments: To keep the summary concise, I

teaching.audioText: To keep the summary concise, I will mention only two findings.

prompt.es: Escribe el mini informe: objetivo, resultados con cifras, un matiz y una recomendación.

answer.text: The aim of this report is to describe how students travel to school. The method was a survey of 100 students. The main findings show that 52 percent of respondents come by school bus, whereas only 6 percent cycle. Furthermore, 35 students said that the bus journey takes more than forty minutes. It appears that long journeys may be a problem for students who live far away, although more evidence is needed. The conclusion is that the school bus is the most common way to travel. Therefore, it is recommended that the school should consider a second morning bus, which would probably shorten the commute.
accepted: The aim of this report is to describe how students travel to school. The method was a survey of 100 students. The main findings show that 52 percent of respondents come by school bus, whereas only 6 percent cycle. Furthermore, 35 students said that the bus journey takes more than forty minutes. It appears that long journeys may be a problem for students who live far away, although more evidence is needed. The conclusion is that the school bus is the most common way to travel. Therefore, it is recommended that the school should consider a second morning bus, which would probably shorten the commute.

This report gives an overview of how students get to school. A survey of 100 students was carried out. The findings show that more than half of the respondents, 52 percent, use the school bus, while only 6 percent cycle and 12 percent come by car. In addition, 35 students said the journey by bus is longer than forty minutes. There is some evidence that long journeys may affect students who live far away, but it remains unclear how many are affected. To conclude, the bus is the main way to travel. We recommend that the school consider an extra bus in the morning.

feedback.es: El mini informe lleva el objetivo, dos resultados con cifras, una afirmación matizada y una recomendación, con tono neutro.

origin.text: Encuesta del consejo escolar a 100 estudiantes sobre cómo llegan al colegio: 52 en autobús escolar, 30 a pie, 12 en coche y 6 en bicicleta. El viaje en autobús dura más de 40 minutos para 35 estudiantes. Escribe entre 100 y 170 palabras: el objetivo, dos resultados con cifras, una afirmación matizada y una recomendación.

prompt.es: Escribe el resumen oral de un minuto con anuncio, punto clave, cautela y recomendación.

answer.text: I will outline the main findings of our survey on digital habits. The key point is that 64 of the 80 students use a phone for more than three hours a day. Only a minority, 20 students, sleep fewer than seven hours. It appears that heavy users tend to sleep less, although more evidence is needed. To conclude, we recommend a phone-free hour before bed.
accepted: I will outline the main findings of our survey on digital habits. The key point is that 64 of the 80 students use a phone for more than three hours a day. Only a minority, 20 students, sleep fewer than seven hours. It appears that heavy users tend to sleep less, although more evidence is needed. To conclude, we recommend a phone-free hour before bed.

I will briefly present our survey on digital habits. The main point is that most students, 64 out of 80, use a phone for more than three hours daily. It seems that heavy users may sleep less, but we cannot be sure. Only 20 students sleep fewer than seven hours. In conclusion, we recommend one hour without phones before bed.

feedback.es: El resumen anuncia, da el punto clave con una cifra, añade una cautela y cierra con una recomendación, en frases cortas.

origin.text: Encuesta sobre hábitos digitales (80 estudiantes): 64 usan el móvil más de tres horas al día; solo 20 duermen menos de siete horas; los que más lo usan parecen dormir menos.
